why: The lookahead's rung from search-51 (#387). A lookahead guessing the other side as search-51 beats search-51 0.655 on unseen seeds where the plain lookahead took 0.37, and one evaluating and guessing with search-51's weights beats it 0.615 (journal, 2026-11-01): the lookahead climbs with the weights it guesses with. This rung searches the lookahead's own weights, starting from search-51's, as `lookahead:<candidate>`, which both evaluates and guesses with the candidate. Every candidate plays search-51 and, on its first 20 seeds, the table's first seat (`lookahead:heuristic:learning/weights/search-51.json`), so a set cannot climb by learning the one-move player alone and the dear lookahead seat stays affordable; the hold-out replays both on every seed. 60 seeds drawn fresh from 7000000 to 7900000 (lookahead-rung-seeds-60-7m.json), a window no run has used, nor the hold-out window just above it. 4 rounds of 8, seed 0, no check opponent, as #359. What would make it a rung: a set that beats search-51's weights as a lookahead against both search-51 and the table's first seat on the unseen seeds the hold-out replays, and the first seat itself.
